rationale: A consistently links behavior to inputs (touch t=8, call t=20, food t=32, present ball t=44, startle t=68, withdraw-attention t=84) and also makes sensible self-initiated shifts (e.g., turns to buzzer at t=30 without input; play-bow to cube t=42; shifts to chime t=54; re-engages play t=78; looks to ball t=94). B responds to touch, food, and startle but ignores the call (t=20) and the presented ball (t=44), and spends long stretches with attention=NONE (t=40–67, 72–95) despite stimuli. A’s timeline shows more autonomous, coherent, and adaptive activity, indicating greater apparent aliveness.
